facts.history: As a new organisation, EACH is building a foundation for plant conservation, herbarium development and botanical knowledge. Its starting priorities are to establish careful documentation, prepare accessible learning resources and develop respectful ways of working with knowledge holders. These priorities describe the work ahead, without claiming a history of completed projects.
facts.title: Plants, knowledge and a new beginning
facts.description: EACH is a new organisation with an East African focus, beginning in Uganda. Its first priorities connect botanical documentation, conservation learning and responsible community participation.
facts.photography: Licensed reference photography; not documentation of EACH activities

changes.lead: Mission: To support the conservation of East Africa's plant diversity through botanical documentation, herbarium development, education and respectful collaboration with knowledge holders. Vision: An East Africa where plant diversity and the knowledge associated with it are valued, responsibly documented and safeguarded for future generations.

principles.title: Values and strategic objectives
principles.description: These principles guide EACH's botanical documentation, learning resources and approach to collaboration.

items.title: Scientific care
items.body: Build botanical records that can be checked, with sources, identification notes and clear limits.

items.title: Conservation responsibility
items.body: Use botanical evidence to inform the care of plants and habitats; distinguish intentions from demonstrated results.

items.title: Respect for knowledge holders
items.body: Seek informed consent, agree attribution and access, and respect community decisions about sensitive knowledge.

items.title: Learning and participation
items.body: Develop educational material and opportunities for people to contribute with appropriate guidance.

items.title: Responsible access
items.body: Share useful knowledge while protecting privacy, restricted community knowledge and sensitive species information.

items.title: Accountable collaboration
items.body: Define responsibilities between independent organisations and report activities with evidence.

changes.title: Leadership and accountability
changes.lead: Scientific care, responsible stewardship and clear responsibilities guide the development of EACH. Governance is described here through its responsibilities; no unverified personal profiles or board appointments are presented.

invitation.description: Collaboration connects botanical expertise, community priorities and opportunities for learning. Each relationship should have a clear purpose, agreed responsibilities and respect for organisational independence.

types.title: Ways independent organisations can work together

steps.text: Collaboration begins with a shared purpose and a clear scope. Independent organisations agree responsibilities, permissions, resources, reporting and arrangements for knowledge and data before work starts. Research, conservation, community and education partnerships are part of this framework; no additional signed partnerships are claimed. Official contact and location details are being confirmed.

profile.description: Bitwiire Herbarium Cafe and EACH retain their own identities and responsibilities.
profile.text: Bitwiire Herbarium Cafe is an independent partner of East African Community Herbariums (EACH). The organisations are separate: neither owns or runs the other. This profile describes that relationship without making claims about services, staff, qualifications or activities. Official visiting and contact details are being confirmed.

programmes.title: Four connected areas of focus
programmes.description: Plant conservation, environmental conservation, medicinal plant knowledge and indigenous knowledge shape EACH's starter plans. These fields connect documentation, habitat awareness, responsible research and education.

status.title: Developing the herbarium foundation
status.text: Herbarium development is one of EACH's founding priorities. Its starter documentation project focuses on record standards, identification evidence and the requirements for responsible curation. The reference sheets shown here illustrate herbarium methods; they do not establish that EACH owns or manages a physical collection. No EACH specimen inventory is presented on this website.

changes.title: Resources

items.title: Botanical identity
items.body: Record a scientific identification and the evidence supporting it; local names alone may be ambiguous.

items.title: Cultural context
items.body: Attribute a reported use to its source and setting, with permission. A reported traditional use is not proof of safety or effectiveness.

items.title: Permission and access
items.body: Agree what may be recorded, retained and shared before collecting knowledge; respect restrictions and intellectual property rights.

items.title: Conservation care
items.body: Consider whether proposed research or collection could put wild plants or sensitive knowledge at risk.

principles.title: A starting point for agreement with knowledge holders

items.title: Informed agreement
items.body: Explain the proposed purpose, recording methods, access and intended uses in an accessible language before seeking consent.

items.title: Custodian-led attribution
items.body: Agree whether and how individuals and communities wish to be acknowledged; do not publish identities by default.

items.title: Control over sharing
items.body: Agree restrictions, storage, reuse and a workable process for changing or withdrawing permission, including limits after publication.

items.title: Fair arrangements
items.body: Discuss benefits, responsibilities and applicable access requirements before work starts; document mutually agreed terms where required.

principles.details: The community knowledge dialogue project starts with listening and agreement about purpose, attribution, access and benefit-sharing. No community consent is presumed, and no restricted knowledge will be collected or published before the relevant permissions and terms are agreed.

changes.body:
## About this notice
This notice describes the website's current functions. EACH is responsible for its editorial content; Wilsoft Technologies provides development services. Official privacy contact details and locations are being confirmed. This notice does not claim regulatory certification or establish a verified retention schedule.

## Public pages
The public website provides informational pages. Public enquiry, volunteer and partnership forms, newsletter registration and public user accounts are not currently provided.

## Restricted staff access
Authorised staff use a restricted CMS. Neon Managed Auth provides staff authentication and session cookies. CMS records include staff membership and roles, editorial changes and audit events used to operate restricted access and the editorial workflow.

## Infrastructure and technical information
The implementation uses Neon for its database, managed authentication and private object storage. Services delivering the website may process connection and request information. This notice makes no unverified promise about provider retention periods, processing locations or deletion procedures. Those arrangements must be reflected in the notice as the service changes.

## Published content and external links
Personal information is published only through the applicable editorial and permission controls. Reference photographs, specimen records and educational sources link to external services with their own privacy notices. No advertising or analytics integration was identified in this repository; that is not a guarantee about every external service.

## Contact and future features
Official privacy and accessibility channels will appear on the [contact page](/contact) when confirmed. Do not treat that page as an operational enquiry form. Before public collection forms or tracking are introduced, this notice must describe the actual fields, purposes, recipients, access and retention arrangements.
changes.title: Privacy
changes.description: How the EACH website handles public content, restricted staff access and technical information.

changes.body:
## About the website
This website presents information about East African Community Herbariums (EACH), plant conservation and botanical knowledge. EACH is a new organisation. Its starter projects are plans, not completed case studies or evidence of achieved results.

## Educational information
Plant information is for education and conservation. It is not medical advice and does not establish that a plant or traditional preparation is safe or effective. Consult a qualified health professional about health concerns.

## Material and permissions
Third-party photographs and specimen images retain their stated credits and licences. Reuse must follow the applicable licence. No blanket licence is granted over all text, community knowledge, personal information or brand assets. Use of EACH and Bitwiire names and logos requires the relevant rights holder's permission.

## Independent organisations and external references
EACH and Bitwiire Herbarium Cafe are independent: neither owns or runs the other. External botanical and conservation sources are attributed to their original institutions; a reference link does not establish an EACH partnership or endorsement.

## Services and project plans
This website does not currently provide public enquiry or application forms, a searchable EACH specimen catalogue, medical services or research-access agreements. Project plans describe intended work subject to practical arrangements, permissions and responsible participation.

## Contact and changes
Official contact and location details are being confirmed on the [contact page](/contact). These terms may be updated as the website's functions change. No regulatory compliance or unverified legal registration claim is made here.

mosaics.details: The plant learning resources project will prepare introductory material connecting plants with habitats, water, soil and responsible environmental observation. Educational work will be distinguished from habitat restoration or measured conservation outcomes.

changes.body:
## How the website is built
Pages use headings, landmarks and lists. Keyboard focus and a skip link support navigation. Images have text alternatives or are decorative. Reduced-motion preferences are respected, and content is available without JavaScript.

## Testing and limits
Development checks include axe scans, keyboard use, responsive layouts, reduced motion and pages without JavaScript. Automated checks do not establish universal usability or certify conformance. A manual screen-reader audit remains part of the future quality milestone.

## Feedback
An official accessibility contact and response target are being confirmed. Once available, feedback can identify the page and task that was difficult, without including sensitive personal information.
